look_here_first: START WITH LOW, SMOOTH, AND ROUND. Fendler's sandmat (E. fendleri) is a small perennial with clustered prostrate to ascending GLABROUS stems from a woody thickened crown (woody root not photographed in any cleared public photo yet). Leaves are opposite, small, broad and rounded-to-ovate, with ENTIRE margins rather than the narrow linear blades of E. angusta. Look closely for glabrous 3-lobed green capsule and distinct linear stipules. True photographed detached seeds are pale and strongly FOUR-ANGLED, with slight wrinkles and occasional depressions, NOT regular prominent transverse seed ridges. Compare E. serpens (tiny annual mat with fused scale stipules) and E. angusta (erect, narrow, strigose leaves); cyathial gland appendage size and color are highly variable and should not lead the identification. Formal BONAP/NAPA native-by-county badge remains on hold.

key_traits.label: Family pattern
key_traits.text: Euphorbia sect. Anisophyllum sandmat. Habit longevity, stipules, leaf margins, capsule surface, and seed form are more reliable than gland-appendage shape.

key_traits.label: Growth form
key_traits.text: Perennial with woody, thickened taproot; stems usually prostrate, decumbent, or ascending, very rarely erect, densely clustered from the woody crown, about 5–12 cm.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Usually opposite, rarely whorled; blades typically orbiculate to ovate, rarely almost lanceolate, about 3–8 × 2.5–7 mm; base slightly asymmetric and slightly cordate to rounded/obtuse; margins entire; surfaces glabrous.

key_traits.label: Stipules
key_traits.text: Distinct, narrowly linear, about 0.5–1 mm, glabrous.

key_traits.label: Cyathium
key_traits.text: Solitary at distal nodes. Four yellow-green to reddish glands; appendages absent or white/pink and highly variable in size/shape, so appendage form should not be used as a primary ID character.

key_traits.label: Seed
key_traits.text: Seeds white, ovoid-pyramidal, prominently 4-angled in cross section, about 1.7–2 × 1–1.2 mm, smooth to slightly wrinkled.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: dense cluster of very low glabrous stems

lookalikes.differences: Against the tiny annual sandmats, the woody perennial base is a major clue. Against E. angusta, E. fendleri stays low and has short rounded leaves; E. angusta is erect with very narrow distal leaves. Do not lean heavily on involucral gland appendage shape because it is variable in E. fendleri.
